summary: The sample implements the requested Python LangChain RAG triage chatbot, creates a server-side DiskANN vector index, seeds deterministic embeddings for offline testing, and exposes a FastAPI /triage endpoint that returns structured triage advice. Core functional requirements were met and unit tests were executed in this run. Findings: (1) some gallery expectations around documentation, test strategy, dependency pinning and error handling were not fully implemented; (2) a few best-practice checks from the product skills were read but not surfaced in the README or tests (index-tuning guidance, offline test strategy, handling embedding failures). See requirement_results and checks for details and minimal fixes.

requirement_results.requirement: Implement the chatbot in Python with LangChain as a RAG pipeline that accepts a free-text symptom description and returns triage advice.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app.py lines 65-72 (POST /triage endpoint) and lines 35-62 (llm_generate using LangChain ChatOpenAI when available, fallback otherwise).

requirement_results.requirement: Store the clinical triage guideline sections as documents in Azure DocumentDB with an embedding on each document and create a cosmosSearch vector index on the embedding field with matching dimensions.
requirement_results.evidence: app/seed.py lines 16-26 (create_index with cosmosSearchOptions kind:'vector-diskann', dimensions from EMBEDDING_DIMS) and lines 43-52 (upsert documents including embedding, embeddingModel, embeddingDims).

requirement_results.requirement: For each symptom description, embed the description with the same embedding model and retrieve the most relevant guideline sections with a $search / cosmosSearch query so the similarity runs in Azure DocumentDB.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app.py lines 74-84 (get_embedding then $search / cosmosSearch pipeline) and app/utils.py lines 41-57 (get_embedding returns normalized vector, uses EMBEDDING_MODEL and EMBEDDING_DIMS).

requirement_results.requirement: Pass the retrieved guideline sections into the LangChain prompt as the context the generated answer is grounded in.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app.py lines 47-50 (context_text built from retrieved contexts) and lines 51-56 (ChatOpenAI call).

requirement_results.requirement: Enforce the safety guardrails through prompt engineering in the LangChain prompt template: every response recommends professional consultation and never gives a diagnosis.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app.py lines 42-46 (system prompt explicitly: 'Do NOT provide medical diagnoses. Always recommend ... consult a qualified healthcare professional ...') and app/utils.py lines 71-75 (deterministic fallback also enforces guardrails).

requirement_results.requirement: Return the triage advice as a structured output (e.g. a Pydantic model or JSON object) that includes an urgency level alongside the advice.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app.py defines Pydantic models SourceItem (lines 23-27) and TriageResponse (lines 29-32) and returns TriageResponse at lines 116-118.

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/db.py lines 9-13 (DOCUMENTDB_URI read from environment) and app/.env.example lines 3-6 (DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY placeholders).

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lines 3-10 list DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIMS and LLM_MODEL.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: app/utils.py lines 12-13 set EMBEDDING_MODEL='text-embedding-3-small' and EMBEDDING_DIMS=1536; seed.py line 21 creates the index with dimensions=EMBEDDING_DIMS (1536).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: app/seed.py lines 19-25 pick moderate DiskANN params (maxDegree=32, lBuild=50); README (app/README.md) does not explain how to tune these parameters for larger corpora.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add an 'Index tuning' section to README explaining the chosen defaults and how to change maxDegree / lBuild / lSearch / k for larger datasets (one paragraph and example values).

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/db.py implements a module-level singleton _client and get_client() (lines 4-13) and app/app.py calls get_client() at runtime (line 71).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/seed.py uses coll.create_index (idempotent attempt) lines 12-27 and coll.update_one(..., upsert=True) line 52 to upsert documents.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app.py lines 68-69 return HTTP 400 for empty 'symptoms'. There is no explicit try/except around get_embedding(symptoms) (line 74) to return a clear error if an embedding provider call fails.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Wrap the embedding call in try/except and raise HTTPException(502, 'Embedding provider failed: ...') with a short error message when get_embedding raises an exception.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app.py $project stage sets 'score': {'$meta': 'searchScore'} (lines 88-95) and contexts include score (lines 106-112).

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: app/requirements.txt contains unpinned dependencies (fastapi, uvicorn, python-dotenv, openai, langchain, pydantic, pytest, requests) and only a loose constraint for pymongo (pymongo>=4.3).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Pin exact package versions in requirements.txt (e.g., fastapi==0.XX.X, uvicorn==X.Y.Z, pymongo==4.20.1, etc.).

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: app/tests/test_app.py executes seed() (lines 22-26) which upserts into the real cluster via get_client(); tests therefore rely on a reachable cluster in this repo's test setup.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Provide test fixtures that either (a) monkeypatch get_client() to return a local in-memory or mocked client, or (b) document and include a small script to run the DocumentDB local gateway container in CI and point DOCUMENTDB_URI at it; update tests to use the fixture.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: Repository contains no Bicep / ARM / Terraform / AzAPI files for Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add an IaC snippet (Bicep or Terraform/AzAPI) demonstrating Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with default low-cost parameters and a comment about changing tier/region.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md lines 1-7 (what this sample shows), lines 9-12 (prerequisites), lines 20-26 (install & seed), and lines 35-36 (clean-up).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample runs with the commands in the README.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md lines 20-29 list pip install, python seed.py, and uvicorn app:app --reload; the run log shows these commands were used during verification (events: run_command for pip install and python seed.py).

requirement_results.requirement: Tests exist and pass without a live cloud resource, or the README says what they need.
requirement_results.evidence: Tests exist (app/tests/test_app.py) and README (app/README.md lines 9-12) documents prerequisites including DOCUMENTDB_URI and optional OPENAI_API_KEY; tests were run in this run and passed given the available cluster.

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name 'Azure DocumentDB' throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md line 1 and other files reference 'Azure DocumentDB' consistently; .env.example uses the mongocluster hostname style.

checks.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable at runtime and never commit connection strings or secrets to source control.
checks.evidence: app/db.py lines 9-13 read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment; app/.env.example line 3 shows a placeholder URI.
checks.source: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

sources.title: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

checks.practice: Create and reuse a single long-lived MongoClient instance (one client per process) so drivers reuse connection pools instead of creating a client for each request.
checks.evidence: app/db.py lines 4-13 implements a process-wide _client singleton and get_client(); app/app.py calls get_client() at runtime (line 71).

checks.practice: Explicitly tune client connection parameters (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS, maxPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS) to bound resources and fail fast rather than relying on driver defaults.
checks.evidence: app/db.py creates MongoClient(uri, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000) (line 13) thereby setting serverSelectionTimeoutMS; more explicit poolSize tuning is not present (no maxPoolSize config).
checks.source: Query from any node in Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: If desired, add explicit maxPoolSize and maxIdleTimeMS (e.g., MongoClient(uri, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, maxPoolSize=20)).

checks.practice: Require TLS for all client connections and validate server certificates (use tls=true / sslmode=verify-full).
checks.evidence: app/db.py relies on the provided connection URI (line 13) but the code does not explicitly validate that TLS is required or reject insecure options (no parsing/validation to forbid tlsAllowInvalidCertificates). .env.example uses mongodb+srv host but that alone does not enforce certificate validation in code.
checks.source: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (rest-api)
checks.fix: Add validation after reading DOCUMENTDB_URI: parse the URI and reject connection strings that allow invalid certs; document in README to always use TLS and avoid tlsAllowInvalidCertificates.

sources.title: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (rest-api)

checks.practice: Use least-privilege credentials for application access: create nonadministrative users/roles with only the minimum DB privileges required instead of using admin/master credentials.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example shows a placeholder connection string (line 3) but repository does not indicate whether the example or the user's configured DOCUMENTDB_URI should be least-privilege; cannot determine credential privilege from code.
checks.source: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (rest-api)
checks.fix: Document a recommended practice in README to create and use a non-admin DB user or managed identity for runtime and a separate admin user for seeding, with a short example.

sources.title: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (rest-api)

decision_reviews.comment: Approval with 'ready_with_gaps' is consistent with the builder's final state (sample built but with documentation/test gaps). The decision was recorded (decisions.jsonl) and the events trace shows a readiness/build flow.
Choosing Python + FastAPI is consistent with the code produced (app/app.py). The decision reason_source was 'prompt' and is supported by the repository.
Choosing pymongo and a singleton MongoClient is implemented in app/db.py; the documentdb-driver skill was loaded (events.jsonl) and the code follows that guidance.

Selecting OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) is implemented: utils.py defaults and seed.py use EMBEDDING_DIMS=1536. The decision is consistent with the readiness review and the vector index creation.

Using OpenAI gpt-3.5-turbo via LangChain with a deterministic fallback is implemented: app/app.py conditionally imports LangChain ChatOpenAI and falls back to generate_response_with_fallback when OPENAI_API_KEY or LangChain are not available.

Creating a server-side DiskANN index was carried out and verified: seed.py creates the index, and the run produced a documentdb_list_indexes result showing 'guidelines_embedding_diskann' with the requested cosmosSearchOptions.

Reading the connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI and not storing secrets in repo is implemented in app/db.py and .env.example. The events trace shows the environment and run used the provided cluster.

Choosing a small synthetic corpus and idempotent seed script is implemented (app/sample_data.py and app/seed.py). The decision's reason_source was 'model_default' originally but the result is safe and documented in README as synthetic sample data.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Explicit pinned versions in requirements.txt (the repo uses unpinned dependencies).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository files (app/requirements.txt) and the build logs/events (events.jsonl show pip install used cached wheels but no pinned file).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Lack of pinned dependencies increases reproducibility risk (tests/install may install different versions in CI) and can cause subtle behavioral differences across environments.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add pinned requirements.txt (requirements.txt) with explicit versions. Example: fastapi==0.95.0, uvicorn==0.23.0, pymongo==4.20.1, python-dotenv==1.2.4, openai==0.29.0, langchain==0.1.0, pydantic==1.10.11, pytest==7.4.0, requests==2.31.0. Also add a short note in README explaining how to rebuild the virtualenv.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A test strategy and CI-friendly fixtures that run tests without a live production cluster (mocking get_client or using the DocumentDB local gateway).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository tests, README and documentdb-local-deployment skill resources (events.jsonl show that skill was loaded but no test fixtures were added).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Tests in this repo run against a reachable cluster in the run environment; they are not portable to CI environments that should not use production secrets, so CI would either need a test cluster or the tests would fail/misuse credentials.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide one of: (A) a pytest fixture that monkeypatches app.db.get_client() to return a local in-memory or mongomock client for unit tests; (B) a small script & docker-compose to run the DocumentDB local gateway for integration tests and instructions to point DOCUMENTDB_URI at localhost:10260 for CI; include example CI steps that use the fixture/matcher.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: README lacks guidance on how to tune DiskANN/HNSW/IVF parameters (maxDegree, lBuild, lSearch, numLists) for larger datasets.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository README and seed.py. The documentdb-vector-search skill and its 'vector-create-diskann-index.md' resource provide tuning heuristics (events.jsonl shows the skill resource was read).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample used moderate defaults appropriate for ~20 docs, but users may copy these defaults into production without tuning, potentially causing poor recall or excessive resource use.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an 'Index tuning' subsection in README summarizing: why dimensions must match embedding model; recommended defaults for small demos (DiskANN: maxDegree=32, lBuild=50, lSearch=50), how to increase lSearch for recall, and links to the vector-search docs for large-corpus production tuning.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Explicit server-side handling and user-facing error messages when external embedding provider calls fail.
doc_gaps.where_searched: app/app.py and app/utils.py (no try/except around get_embedding in app), and standard LangChain/OpenAI docs. The run logs show real OpenAI calls were not executed in this run and fallback was used.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: If OPENAI_API_KEY is set in a user's environment and the embedding call fails (network/quotas), the current endpoint would raise a server-side exception and return a generic 500 without a clear indication that the embedding provider failed.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add try/except around get_embedding() in the /triage handler; on failure return HTTP 502 with 'Embedding provider failed' and include a short remediation sentence. Add a unit test asserting the 502 response when the embedding call raises.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: An example Bicep/Terraform snippet that demonstrates creating an Azure DocumentDB (mongoClusters) cluster using the Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource type.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repository root (no IaC files) and readiness notes that provisioning was intentionally omitted (run environment told builder not to create clusters).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Users who want to reproduce the end-to-end sample must already have a cluster; providing IaC lowers friction and prevents users from choosing the wrong (databaseAccounts / RU) resource type.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a minimal 'infra/' directory with a Bicep and/or Terraform AzAPI example showing Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameters (tier=M30 default, storage minimal, region variable). Document the difference between mongoClusters and databaseAccounts.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The decision to use synthetic guideline text was recorded with reason_source 'model_default'.
doc_gaps.where_searched: decisions.jsonl (D008) and README; the sample does include synthetic data but the choice originated from a model_default decision entry.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: While using synthetic data is safe, a model_default origin means the agent's default led the choice. Making this guidance explicit in a developer-facing doc prevents ambiguity about when to use synthetic vs licensed clinical content and what approvals are required.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short section in README or a contributor guide: 'Why synthetic data?': explain licensing/PHI reasons, when to swap in real guidelines, and the governance/clinical-review checklist required before using real clinical content.
